samir: FYI customer on Next.js SSR (server-side render, not edge) started getting 401s after upgrading node SDK to v1.4.0. Only happens when they build with Turbopack. Repro steps below.

maya: thanks — can you paste package.json + exports map and the runtime error log? also which Node version on Vercel?

samir: package.json snippet:
```
"dependencies": {
  "redwood-inference": "^1.4.0",
  "next": "13.5.2"
},
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  }
}
```
node runtime error from Vercel build output:
```
Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: No "./dist/esm/index.js" export main defined in package.json imported from /vercel/path/.next/server/pages/index.js
    at new NodeError (internal/errors.js:363:5)
    at packageExportsResolve (internal/modules/esm/resolve.js:...),
    at new Loader
```
and the app then receives 401 when calling the API (looks like missing auth header due to bundler tree-shake?). Customer confirms local dev `next dev` works fine, only production build + turbopack.

eli: hmm — two suspects: (1) bundler is resolving to the ESM entry but tree-shaking removed the export that attaches auth shim, or (2) the exports map lacks the fallback path turbopack expects. Turbopack can be aggressive. Quick check: can they try `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` vs `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` in compiled server bundle? also what does the bundled file look like (`.next/server/...`)?

samir: tried changing import style, no change. I found a minimal repro: create a tiny next server route that imports the SDK and does `new Client({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })` — build fails with the package-path-not-exported error. Local `node -r esm` works.

maya: can you also paste `tsconfig`/`next.config.js`? any custom `externals`? and node version on Vercel (they're on 18.x).

samir: next.config.js uses default, no externals. Node 18.16.0. tsconfig target es2020.

eli: likely root cause: package's exports map points to `./dist/esm/index.js` but we forgot to include the path in the published package (packaging/rollup config only emitted `index.mjs` with different path). So when Turbopack resolves the import specifier it hits exports map mismatch -> runtime resolution error. In some builds that falls back to cjs but here turbopack follows exports strictly.

support-bot: Deploy 0c3f2b4 (customer-prod) failed build on Vercel — see https://vercel.co/jobs/0c3f2b4

maya: customer can downgrade to 1.3.9 (confirmed) while we cut a patch. ask them to set `npm i redwood-inference@1.3.9` as a temporary mitigation. we'll prepare 1.4.1 with fixed exports mapping.

samir: downgrading to 1.3.9 resolves — thanks. Would be great to have a short repro that we can run in CI to catch this.

eli: I'll open a small test in repo infra-packaging to replicate turbopack build with `npm pack` produced tarball. plan: (1) adjust rollup to include both `./dist/esm/index.js` and `./dist/esm/index.mjs` paths, (2) ensure `files` in package.json includes exact emitted filenames, (3) add CI job that installs package via `npm pack` and runs `next build` with turbopack enabled.

maya: added customer note with workaround and ETA for patch (2h) :thumbsup:

samir: thanks — linking the customer thread.

eli: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4123 — will ship patch and cut 1.4.1. also adding a short doc in dev-ex about packaging checks.

infra-bot: CI job turbopack-pack-test started (#834)
